questions.q: What does an Opportunity object represent?
options: A real, in-progress or closed deal, with a dollar value and target close date
An unqualified prospect before any real deal exists
A company or organization
A support ticket
questions.explain: Opportunity tracks a genuine sales pursuit, distinct from a Lead's unqualified inquiry.

questions.q: Which Opportunity field defines the sales pipeline itself and is used to group open deals?
options: Stage
Rating
Lead Source
Account Name
questions.explain: Stage (Prospecting, Qualification, Proposal, Negotiation, Closed Won/Lost) is what defines and organizes the pipeline.

questions.q: Which Opportunity field is summed to calculate "total pipeline value"?
options: Amount
Probability
Close Date
Status
questions.explain: Amount is the deal's dollar value, the figure summed for pipeline value or closed revenue.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what exactly is "the sales pipeline"?
options: Not a separate object — just the set of open Opportunities (Stage not yet Closed Won/Lost), typically grouped by Stage
A dedicated Salesforce object called Pipeline, separate from Opportunity
A field on the Account object
A report that exists independently of any underlying data
questions.explain: The pipeline is simply open Opportunity records, usually visualized grouped by Stage — not a separate data structure.

questions.q: What does the Probability field on an Opportunity represent?
options: An estimated likelihood of the deal closing, often tied automatically to Stage
The exact dollar amount of the deal
The Lead Source of the original inquiry
Whether the Account is a Business Account or Person Account
questions.explain: Probability is a percentage estimate of close likelihood, typically defaulted by Stage but overridable per record.
